prompt:
Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: wide GitHub README banner for otto, an open-source terminal tool that runs coding agents on a schedule, using the scheduler the operating system already has. Landscape approximately 2.4:1.
Primary request: a weekly timetable as a physical object, expressing work that shows up on schedule with nobody watching, and a record of how each run went. Original refined editorial identity, instantly legible and specific to developers. It must look like a sibling of an existing banner: a top-down charcoal organizer tray on warm ivory paper with one mustard-yellow accent piece and a wordmark on the left.
Composition: top-down view of ONE beautifully designed charcoal timetable board on warm ivory paper. The board dominates the right two-thirds. Left third carries the large clear lowercase word "otto", charcoal, precise mature technical typography, with a small mustard terminal prompt symbol (a chevron and an underscore) to its left. Generous clean margin around the wordmark. No other text anywhere.
The board: a shallow matte charcoal tray divided into seven equal vertical lanes, one per day of the week, with fine engraved horizontal hour ticks and no numerals or letters. Small fitted charcoal task cards sit in the lanes at different heights, like appointments on a timetable; each card carries only a tiny engraved pictogram and no text: a terminal prompt on most, a branching git diagram on one, a small document with lines on another. A few cards repeat at the same height across five consecutive lanes, reading as a weekday routine. One slim mustard-yellow bar rides a rail across all seven lanes at one height: the present moment. The single card the bar is crossing is the one running now: a dark terminal tile with a prompt symbol and a small green active dot. Along the bottom edge of the board, a narrow recessed strip holds a tidy row of small round tokens, the record of past runs: most are plain engraved check marks, one is an engraved cross, one is an empty ring. One lane, at the far right, has a small engraved pause mark on its top edge and its cards are set slightly back in their slots: a paused day.
Style: sophisticated technical editorial illustration, overhead industrial design drawing with gently dimensional solid forms, matte surfaces, precise clear geometry, subtle printed grain and restrained soft shadows. A coherent physical object, crafted like a tool organizer. NOT glossy 3D software marketing, NOT a fake software dashboard, NOT a photograph of an actual product.
Palette: warm ivory background, charcoal board and cards, mustard yellow for the time bar only, a tiny green dot for the running card, a muted light paper tone for one or two card faces. Strong tonal separation so the lanes and cards remain understandable when reduced to README width.
Text (verbatim): "otto". Only this word appears, spelled o t t o.
Constraints: no clock face, no alarm clock, no calendar page with numbers, no bus, no mascot, no robots, no brains, no gears, no hourglass, no badges, no percentages, no borrowed brand logos, no Apple logo, no fabricated app UI, no watermark, no gradients or neon glow, no scattered decorative objects outside the board. Avoid plastic toy aesthetic. Exactly seven lanes. The mustard bar is the only yellow object besides the prompt symbol by the wordmark.
